objective: Test whether training-only hard-group weighting improves the selected OCT candidate without reading frozen test images.

hypothesis.statement: The step-20 candidate still confuses NORMAL/DRUSEN and CNV/DME. Upweighting hard training-only patient groups while keeping low-resolution 4-bit QLoRA may improve OCT boundary learning.
hypothesis.result: Not supported. Group weighting changed the teacher-forced loss slightly but did not improve generated-label classification metrics.

validation_audit.note: The screening validation is small and potentially noisy; it cannot replace patient-isolated external validation.

reason: Step 1 lowered validation loss from 0.0350562277 to 0.0350383057, but both task-mean macro-F1 and OCT macro-F1 were unchanged at 0.8733582322 and 0.7915032680.
Steps 2 and 3 did not improve the selection score and triggered early stopping.
The experiment best_adapter is only selected by a marginally lower loss at an identical classification score; it is not a meaningful promotion over the verified step-20 candidate.
The frozen-test promotion gate was not run because no internal-validation candidate exceeded the entry classification metrics.
limitations: The 55-row validation set covers 33 groups and has unequal OCT class counts, so small metric changes are not reliable evidence of generalization.
Training-only hard-group weighting is not independent external validation and cannot resolve source or label limitations.
The frozen OCT test set is not a patient-isolated clinical validation set.
Stage-4 best and final adapters are experiment outputs, not deployment artifacts.
next_step: Stop repeated short continuation runs. Next prioritize model-card/runtime contract work and patient-isolated validation data; only train again after a new data or label hypothesis is available.
